assessments.reasoning: MDC/28 §3.2.3 printed I-10 gives the prior fully specified reference’s name and all preceding subscripts as the saved prefix. The next naked reference supplies its own subscripts. Printed I-11 establishes that the right-hand SET expression can affect the indicator before the left-hand reference.

challenge.method: Trace a qualifying reference to a node with two subscripts followed by a naked reference with one. Check a one-subscript source with an empty saved subscript prefix, an initial naked reference, an unsubscripted fully specified reference, the parent $DATA guard, an intervening reference, and SET order. Compare the rolling YottaDB naked reference guide.
challenge.results: A qualifying two-subscript reference saves its name and first subscript. A one-subscript reference can save the name alone. An initial naked reference is erroneous and an unsubscripted full reference leaves the indicator undefined. The old narrative also leaves it undefined if $DATA on the would-be prefix is below 10. Intervening occurrences and the right side of SET can affect which prefix is in force. The vendor guide’s similar abbreviation is its own implementation documentation.

limitations: The frozen claim is conditional on a defined untouched indicator. The historically specified parent $DATA guard and SET order are distinct from any assumption about vendor behavior.
